content: Post-viral fatigue syndrome (PVFS) is a medical condition characterized by a state of persistent fatigue that arises following a viral infection. This condition is not widely recognized under this specific term, but the phenomenon of prolonged or severe fatigue after an illness is relatively common. Some individuals may experience fatigue and associated symptoms for months or even years after recovering from a severe viral infection. Importantly, PVFS is explicitly excluded from being classified as a neurotic disorder. Within the scope of PVFS, benign myalgic encephalomyelitis (ME) is included. Additionally, alternative diagnoses to ME, such as chronic fatigue syndrome (CFS) and neuromyasthenia, are listed in the International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision (ICD-10). Other post-viral syndromes that may fall under this category include post-polio syndrome, late-stage Lyme disease, and potentially chronic mononucleosis or other severe chronic viral infections. Some researchers propose that post-viral fatigue syndrome represents a biological state of immune system dysfunction, which may involve immune system activation, damage, or weakness. This immune system impairment is thought to be a common feature across various post-viral syndromes. It is hoped that advancements in immune system research, particularly studies related to HIV, may provide insights into the mechanisms underlying post-viral syndromes and lead to the development of effective treatments.
